messages:
emily: Quick UX review for the API Keys page — focusing on the roles/scopes empty state and the create/rotate flow. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx (mock attached). Looking for quick takes on copy, CTAs, and any accessibility nits.

mike: Skimmed — two things jump out: 1) empty state CTA wording feels generic, 2) the role dropdown labels are ambiguous (e.g., 'Full' vs 'Owner'). Suggest we avoid jargon.

sam: engineering note: backend currently has a default of 'full' if no scopes sent. We should avoid creating keys that are accidentally too permissive. Either require explicit scope selection or offer a safe preset.

anya: UX thought: maybe a single primary CTA 'Create a key' then an inline option in the modal for 'Create scoped key' with presets. Keep the empty state simple: headline + supporting sentence + primary CTA.

aiden: accessibility nits: color contrast of the small 'Restricted' badge in the mock is < 3:1 on light bg — needs fix. Also ensure the role dropdown is keyboard accessible and the modal traps focus. Add aria-describedby to the scope helper text.

mike: Proposed empty-state microcopy:

```
Headline: No API keys yet
Body: Create an API key to integrate Redwood with your app. You can choose a preset scope or configure custom permissions later.
Primary CTA: Create API key
Secondary CTA: Create scoped key
```

mike: For role labels I suggest: 'Read-only', 'Embeddings-only', 'Generate + Manage' (instead of Full/Owner). Those map more to actual behaviors.

emily: I like the clearer labels. Also product asks we surface the most common presets first (Read-only, Generate). For enterprise customers we can show 'Custom' last.

sam: Implementation plan: we can add a boolean `require_scope` flag for the creation endpoint. If true, UI must send a selected preset or custom list. We can default `require_scope=true` for new orgs to prevent accidental wide keys. I'll create a ticket.

anya: Minor UI tweak: show the CTA in the empty state as a filled primary button and a text link for the secondary. Also include a tiny hint link: 'What do scopes mean?' that opens a short tooltip.

aiden: Accessibility checklist I'm proposing:
- Ensure contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text
- Badges >= 3:1 on all themes
- Modal: focus trap + first focusable element is the key name input
- Dropdowns: aria-label and keyboard nav tests
- Provide concise helper text and aria-describedby for the scope presets

deploy-bot: Heads-up: copy-only change scheduled in the docs deploy on 2026-04-01 11:30 PT. Backend changes not included in that deploy.

emily: OK — next steps: @mike please produce a microcopy pass and update the empty-state art with the suggested CTAs and the 'What do scopes mean?' link. @sam please file the backend ticket for `require_scope` + presets and tag infra. @aiden and @anya can you pair on the small a11y checklist and send me a quick sign-off when done? :thumbsup:

mike: Will do, I'll post a small diff later today.

sam: Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123 — includes migration notes and defaulting rules.

anya: I'll mock the updated empty state and modal copy in Figma and ping here when ready.

aiden: I'll run the quick contrast checks and keyboard walkthrough once the mock is posted.

emily: Thanks team — keeping this small and iterative. If anyone thinks the primary CTA should be 'Create scoped key' instead of generic 'Create API key', call it out now.

mike: My vote: keep 'Create API key' primary, because it's the familiar pattern, but make the modal default to the safer preset selection.

emily: Agreed. Closing thread after the copy diff is posted.
